newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Progressive to spend NZ$25 mln on systems.
newsitem.headline: Progressive to spend NZ$25 mln on systems.

text.p: Supermarket owner Progressive Enterprises Ltd said on Wednesday it would spend about NZ$25 million over two to three years in a major systems upgrade.

"As a consequence of a review of business practices and processes, recommendations have been accepted by the Board in respect of major systems changes including the acquisition of new point of sale equipment and computer upgrades. The implementation of these changes has commenced in the second half and will continue over the next two to three years at a capital cost of approximately $25 million," the company said.
Progressive earlier reported a rise in half-year net profit to NZ$8.02 million from $2.2 million a year earlier.
It said the result stemmed from a substantial improvement in profits from supermarkets and a reduction in costs.
Operating surpluses before interest and tax grew by 45.6 percent in the retail/wholesale divisions, despite a small decline in turnover.
"The problems that surfaced during the first half last year have been rectified and the single management team continues to improve controls and business practices," Progressive said.
Operating losses at the Georgie Pie chain of restaurants were recorded at similar levels to the second half of last year, despite further reductions in sales.
Of the 17 restaurants sold to McDonalds, six had transferred by balance date with the remaining 11 scheduled during the second half.
The group continued the disposal of non-core properties in accordance with the previously announced programme, and said this was running in line with expectations.
These proceeds, in conjunction with cash flow from operations and the Georgie Pie/McDonalds transaction have enabled bank debt to be reduced to $133.8 million from $207.1 million a year ago.
"Given the forecast trend of debt for the group, the directors have determined to suspend the dividend reinvestment plan," Progressive said.
Foodland Associated Ltd owns 58 percent of Progressive. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
